hypotheses.title: Call-Put Implied Volatility Spread with Linear Decay Smoothing
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Direct turnover optimization of Batch 154 Candidate 1 (548306cc, which achieved a spectacular Sharpe of 1.95 and Sub-universe Sharpe of 1.04 with zero self-correlation). While the underlying economic anomaly (informed institutional call accumulation relative to puts) possesses extraordinary predictive power, daily implied volatility fluctuations generated 51.25% turnover, dampening Fitness to 0.95. Applying ts_decay_linear(..., 5) smooths out high-frequency bid-ask bounce in options market quotes, cutting turnover into the 15%-20% sweet spot and triggering the Tulchinsky Fitness multiplier to vault Fitness well above the 1.50 Gold Consultant threshold.
confounders: Sudden corporate earnings releases altering implied volatility surfaces
hypotheses.falsification_test: Alpha degrades if 5-day linear smoothing introduces excessive lag during fast market selloffs.

candidates.rationale: 30-day ATM call-put volatility spread with 5-day linear decay smoothing and 5-day price reversal overlay

hypotheses.title: 60-Day Tenor Call-Put Volatility Spread (Structural Term Extension)
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Structural term-extension of the 1.95 Sharpe volatility spread anomaly. While 30-day options contracts reflect fast-decaying gamma flow, the 60-day tenor captures longer-term institutional directional positioning. Because 60-day implied volatilities have higher inertia and lower daily percentage variance, turnover is naturally dampened by 30%-40% without compromising the fundamental informativeness of the call-put spread.
confounders: Lower liquidity on 60-day strikes for small-cap equities
Macro index option hedging spilling over into single-stock 60-day skew
hypotheses.falsification_test: Alpha underperforms if institutional informed flow is strictly concentrated in front-month expirations.

candidates.rationale: 60-day ATM call-put volatility spread paired with 5-day short-term price reversal hedge

hypotheses.title: 5-Day Moving Average Call-Put Spread with Expanded Core Allocation
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Filters high-frequency microstructure noise by taking a 5-day rolling average (ts_mean(spread, 5)) of the call-put implied volatility difference, while increasing the core signal allocation to 90% and reducing the short-term reversal overlay to 10%. This dampens churn from both the options spread and the price differencing term, concentrating portfolio weights on persistent institutional sentiment shifts.
confounders: Abrupt gap events diluting 5-day moving averages
Short-term gamma pin risk during expiration week
hypotheses.falsification_test: Alpha underperforms if 5-day rolling averages smooth away critical directional shock information.

candidates.rationale: 5-day moving average smoothed call-put spread with 90% allocation and 10% price reversal buffer
